comments.body:
## Closed not_a_bug by operator decision

The operator reviewed the investigation and dispositioned this **not a bug**. Closing on that
decision, not on new evidence.

**The technical findings in the description are unchanged and were not retracted**, so a future
reader is not misled about what the code does:

- `_mcp_health.py:217` couples uvicorn's `timeout_graceful_shutdown` to the certified-op grace
  (1200s), and the runtime experiment (gauge == 0 in both arms; 0.18s with no open stream vs
  5.39s — the full timeout — with one) shows an open idle stream, not the gauge, pins shutdown.
- Production matched that prediction to the second: stop at 18:25:08, `die` at 18:45:09 = 1200s.
- Consequence: an mcp retirement holds one of the two blue/green ports for the full 20 minutes,
  so a second mcp deploy inside that window hits `AUTODEPLOY_MCP_RETIRE_CAP port-exhausted`
  (`autodeploy.sh:670-674`) and backs off. It fails SAFE — no collision, live backend untouched.

What the not_a_bug disposition settles is the **legitimacy** question the RCA left genuinely
open, and which I flagged as the weakest part of the analysis: the comment
`MCP_STOP_GRACE (1260) >= _mcp_health grace (1200) + margin` shows the author budgeted for a
full-length drain, so waiting out an open client session is defensible as intended conservative
behaviour rather than a defect. That is an operator/design call, and it has been made.

Practical consequence to be aware of rather than surprised by: mcp deploys are effectively
capped at roughly one per 20 minutes whenever a client holds a session. If that ceiling ever
becomes a problem in practice, reopen this ticket — the mechanism and its proof are already
recorded above, so no re-investigation is needed.

The originally-reported symptom ("container Up 2 hours (unhealthy)") was separately confirmed
NOT a defect: `docker ps` "Up" is uptime since creation, that container was the live backend
until the 18:25 cutover, and the retire completed normally in 21 minutes.

Reopened (operator-approved 2026-08-30): the documented reopen condition ("reopen if the 2-port/long-drain ceiling ever becomes a problem in practice") is now proven met by incident 2f46 (`beton-naval-eyas`). In-window: deploy_errors ×11 + mcp-retire-cap ×11 from a landing burst (14 MCP + 142 bot redeploys) hitting port-exhaustion, because uvicorn `timeout_graceful_shutdown` is coupled to the 1200s certified-op grace (`_mcp_health.py:743`) so a retiring MCP container holds a rotation port ~20 min even at 0 in-flight, and there are only 2 ports.

Remediation approved (fixes 1+3; capacity Option 2 deferred): (1) decouple graceful-shutdown from the certified-op grace so a container fast-drains at 0 in-flight; (3) distinguish "bot mid-redeploy" from "bot wedged" before the drain-gate fail-opens (mechanism 2: `bot_in_flight_reviews()` returned -1 on an unreachable /health during the bot's own redeploy). The fix is being driven under bug 2f46 (proven Phase-1; relates_to this ticket). This ticket tracks the design-limitation record.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## DECISION NEEDED — decouple uvicorn's shutdown timeout from the 1200s certified-op drain grace

**The coupling.** `run_http_with_grace` sets uvicorn's `timeout_graceful_shutdown` to the SAME value as the certified-op drain grace (`_mcp_health.py:217`, `= int(grace_seconds)`, `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS = 1200`). For a Streamable-HTTP MCP server a connected client holds a long-lived stream that never closes on its own, so uvicorn waits the full **1200s on every retirement** — and the gauge-driven early exit (`drain_then_exit`, "returns immediately when the gauge is idle", `:134-150`) never fires. The entire `InFlightGauge` apparatus (ADR 0068) is dead in practice.

**The design already intends two separate roles.** The code comments call the gauge the "primary bound" and uvicorn's timeout "a backstop" (`:195`); **ADR 0067 (review-bot-bounded-shutdown)** and **ADR 0069 (bounded-deferral)** establish stop-intake + bounded drain as the model, not one long timer.

**OSS grounding.** Kubernetes separates `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (a hard backstop that force-kills) from the `preStop` drain hook (the app's own, usually shorter, deadline); uvicorn's own docs describe `timeout_graceful_shutdown` as a backstop, not the primary drain.

**Recommendation:** Give uvicorn a short backstop (e.g. 30-60s) and keep 1200s as the certified-op drain deadline enforced by `drain_then_exit`; have the SIGTERM handler stop intake and proactively close IDLE streams so the gauge — not the transport — drives exit. Net: an idle-gauge retirement exits in seconds; a busy one still gets the full certified-op grace. Behavior change → your ruling before I dispatch it.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

Current `origin/main` already contains the bug-2f46 core decoupling: `run_http_with_grace` drives certified-op drain through `InFlightGauge`/`drain_then_exit` and gives uvicorn a separate short graceful-shutdown timeout. This ticket closes the approved 2026-09-01 DECISION by making that separation explicit and durable for the parentless 40a7 bug: name the uvicorn timer as a transport backstop, set its concrete default to 30 seconds, preserve compatibility for existing callers, and add direct tests for the two shutdown directions the incident requires.

The certified-op drain grace remains `DEFAULT_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_SECONDS = 1200`. That value is the primary drain deadline for in-flight certified ops and is enforced by `drain_then_exit`; it is not uvicorn's `timeout_graceful_shutdown`.

Deadline-elapse disposition: if the certified-op drain deadline expires while the gauge is still busy, the retiring process sets `server.should_exit`; uvicorn begins graceful shutdown and the in-flight client receives the terminal shutdown/connection disposition from the transport. That is distinct from the idle path, where `should_exit` is set only after the gauge is already idle and uvicorn's short backstop sweeps idle held-open streams.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` exports `DEFAULT_UVICORN_BACKSTOP_SECONDS = 30` as the named uvicorn transport backstop.
- [x] Existing imports of `DEFAULT_UVICORN_GRACEFUL_SECONDS` remain compatible as an alias for the new backstop constant.
- [x] `run_http_with_grace` passes uvicorn `timeout_graceful_shutdown=int(uvicorn_backstop_seconds)` instead of using the certified-op `grace_seconds` value.
- [x] `run_http_with_grace` preserves the existing keyword `uvicorn_graceful_seconds` as a backward-compatible override for callers while documenting `uvicorn_backstop_seconds` as the preferred name.
- [x] `drain_then_exit` still uses `grace_seconds` as the certified-op drain deadline.
- [x] The SIGTERM handler calls `gauge.begin_draining()` immediately when retirement starts.
- [x] The SIGTERM handler sets `server.should_exit` only after the gauge is idle or the certified-op drain deadline elapses.
- [x] An idle-gauge retirement test proves `server.should_exit` is set immediately/quickly with `grace_seconds=1200`, demonstrating the early-exit path is well under the certified-op grace.
- [x] A busy-gauge retirement test injects a small `grace_seconds` and a shorter uvicorn backstop value and proves `server.should_exit` is not set until the gauge drains or the injected certified-op deadline elapses, so the short uvicorn backstop does not cut short an in-flight certified op.
- [x] The change is self-contained in in-process MCP shutdown logic and does not depend on any CI provider or deployment-specific external service.

## Testing

- Focused: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/interfaces/facades/test_mcp_http_transport.py -k "mcp_retirement or run_http_with_grace or drain_then_exit or sigterm"`
- Lint: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make lint`
- Typecheck: `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make typecheck`
- Gerrit: land only after `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, and no unresolved comments.
